intro.title: Build typed finite workflow graph
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed finite workflow graph to model a simple process, like a user sign-up flow, using TypeScript. You'll learn how to define a graph structure where each node represents a state (e.g., 'start', 'pending', 'complete') and each edge represents a valid transition between states. The core concept involves using TypeScript's type system—specifically, union types and interfaces—to enforce that only allowed transitions can be defined, preventing invalid state changes. This will help you understand how to create type-safe, predictable workflows in your applications.
intro.usecase: Typed finite workflow graphs are essential for modeling predictable state transitions in complex user interfaces. You'll see this pattern in multi-step forms like checkout processes, where each step (shipping → payment → confirmation) must follow specific rules. They're also used in dashboard wizards, approval workflows in admin panels, and interactive data filtering systems where UI states must remain valid and type-safe. As a developer, implementing these graphs ensures your application logic is maintainable, prevents invalid state transitions, and provides clear type definitions for every possible workflow path.
